notes: Parts are the same as step 1; only the button labels were reassigned to match the circuit image, where the leftmost button goes to pin 6 and the rightmost to pin 2. btn1=pin 6 (mouse click), btn2=pin 5 (right), btn3=pin 4 (left), btn4=pin 3 (down), btn5=pin 2 (up). Wire labels are unchanged.

The image shows the breadboard flipped (rows f-j at the top, a-e at the bottom). I mapped the half with rows a-e to bank 't' and the half with rows f-j to bank 'b'. The rail next to the + marking is 'tp' (5V) and the bottom rail's upper row, which the black wire reaches, is 'bn' (GND). Rail hole numbers are approximated by the column they sit beside.

Pushbutton sides: side 1 (1.l/1.r) is the half with rows f-j and is fed from the 5V rail. Side 2 (2.l/2.r) is the half with rows a-e and carries the input pin and the 10k pull-down resistor to GND. Pressing the button takes the input HIGH.

Each signal wire lands in the column of its button's left bottom leg, as does the resistor's top end, so signal, button and pull-down resistor share one strip. Wire 'a' ends go to the Leonardo header sockets (5V, GND.1 and pins 2-6). Wire 'b' ends go to the breadboard.
The USB cable to the computer is not modelled.
